```{r}
#Import the ag data from ITPD-E first
#Main dataset, the ITPD-E
data <- read.csv("ITPDE_R03.CSV")
# Inspect available years and variable names
names(data)
sort(unique(data$year))

# Keep observations from 2012 to 2022. 2012 was chosen because of two reasons: 1) the collection year for NTMs, and 2) the HS2012 codes, so more technical issues can be avoided. The end year coincides with the latest year available.  
us_trade_panel <- data |>
  filter(
    broad_sector == "Agriculture",
    importer_iso3 == "USA",
    year %in% c(2012,2013,2014,2015,2016,2017, 2018, 2019,2020,2021,2022)
  )

# Check observations
us_trade_panel |>
  count(year, name = "observations")

us_trade_panel |>
  summarise(
    exporters = n_distinct(exporter_iso3),
    industries = n_distinct(industry_id),
    years = n_distinct(year)
  )

#Drop forestry and fishing
unique(us_trade_panel$industry_descr)
us_trade_panel <- us_trade_panel %>%
  filter(!industry_descr %in% c("Forestry", "Fishing"))
unique(us_trade_panel$year)
write.csv(
  us_trade_panel,
  "us_trade_panel.csv"
)
us_trade_panel<-read_csv("us_trade_panel.csv")
unique(us_trade_panel$year)
```


```{r}
#Now, create the crosswalk. 
#Next step: See the concordance tables. This table was done manually, using data provided by FAOSTAT. I compared the FCL item with the HS code (HS2012) and created a table which has both, to use as a crosswalk. Sources: 1) https://www.usitc.gov/data/gravity/gravity_portal_itpd_e for the IPTD-E commodity data. 2) https://www.fao.org/statistics/caliper/tools/download/en for the FAOSTAT classification.

concordance_FCL_HS2012<- read_excel("concordance_tableITPDEupdated.xlsx")
unique(concordance_FCL_HS2012$itpd_description)
concordance_FCL_HS2012
#Note: R did not drop leading 0s. 
#Note: this object will be used to aggregate the HS codes later. 

#To make this work: Expand the HS codes. There are rows in which multiple HS codes are written, so make one row per each first. 
itpd_crosswalk <- concordance_FCL_HS2012%>%
  mutate(HS_2012 = as.character(HS_2012)) %>%
  separate_rows(HS_2012, sep = ",\\s*") %>%
  mutate(
    HS6 = str_pad(
      str_trim(HS_2012),
      width = 6,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(HS6), HS6 != "") %>%
  distinct(HS6, itpd_description)
unique(itpd_crosswalk$itpd_description)

#Check that the industries match the ITPD-E industries perfectly

setequal(
  unique(itpd_crosswalk$itpd_description),
  unique(us_trade_panel$industry_descr)
)
#There are rows that have different abbreviations or typos. Manually make them match. 
itpd_crosswalk_final <- itpd_crosswalk %>%
  mutate(
    itpd_description = dplyr::recode(
      itpd_description,
      "Other meats, livest. r. live animals" =
        "Other meats, livestock products, and live animals",
      "Other ag. products, nec" =
        "Other agricultural products, nec",
      "Pulses  legumes(dried, preserved)" =
        "Pulses and legumes, dried, preserved",
      "Other oilseeds (exc. eanuts)" =
        "Other oilseeds (excluding peanuts)",
      "Prepared fruits, fruit juices" =
        "Prepared fruits and fruit juices",
      "Raw  refined sugar  sugar crops" =
        "Raw and refined sugar and sugar crops",
      "Animal feed ingredients pet foods" =
        "Animal feed ingredients and pet foods",
      "Tobacco leaves  cigarettes" =
        "Tobacco leaves and cigarettes"
    )
  )
setequal(
  unique(itpd_crosswalk_final$itpd_description),
  unique(us_trade_panel$industry_descr)
)
#This command returned TRUE, so the crosswalk is complete. 

write_csv(
  itpd_crosswalk_final,
  "itpde_crosswalk.csv"
)

itpd_crosswalk_final<-read.csv("itpde_crosswalk.csv")
```


```{r}
#Now start with NTM data
ntm_file <- normalizePath(
  "NTMs_HS2012Ver_Researcher.csv",
  winslash = "/",
  mustWork = TRUE
)

# Protect the path for use inside SQL
ntm_file_sql <- gsub(
  "'",
  "''",
  ntm_file,
  fixed = TRUE
)

# Open a temporary DuckDB connection
con <- dbConnect(
  duckdb(),
  dbdir = ":memory:"
)

# Read only the column names without importing the data into R
column_names <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste0(
    "DESCRIBE SELECT * ",
    "FROM read_csv_auto('",
    ntm_file_sql,
    "', header = true, all_varchar = true)"
  )
)

print(column_names)

#See the available countries
reporter_values <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste0(
    "SELECT DISTINCT TRIM(\"Reporter\") AS Reporter ",
    "FROM read_csv_auto('",
    ntm_file_sql,
    "', header = true, all_varchar = true) ",
    "ORDER BY Reporter"
  )
)

reporter_values
#Filter for the US
us_ntms <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste0(
    "SELECT * ",
    "FROM read_csv_auto('",
    ntm_file_sql,
    "', header = true, all_varchar = true) ",
    "WHERE TRIM(\"Reporter\") = 'USA'"
  )
)

#See which years are available
unique(us_ntms$Year) #note that the years that appear here are the collection years, not the years in which each NTM was introduced or terminated
unique(us_ntms$MinStartYear) #years in which the NTMs started
unique(us_ntms$MaxEndYear) #years in which the NTMs ended. 

#Now only retain the HS codes present in the crosswalk, as they are the products of interest for each industry
hs_codes_itpde<- itpd_crosswalk_final$HS6
#Now in the NTM data, retain only these values 
us_ntms <- us_ntms %>%
  filter(HSCode %in% hs_codes_itpde)
write_csv(
  us_ntms,
  "us_ntms_raw.csv"
)
us_ntms<-read.csv("us_ntms_raw.csv")

head(us_ntms,500)

#Make sure eveything is in the right type
us_ntms <- us_ntms %>%
  mutate(
    HS6 = str_pad(
      trimws(as.character(HSCode)),
      width = 6,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    ),

    NTMCode = trimws(
      as.character(NTMCode)
    ),

    HSNomenclature = trimws(
      as.character(HSNomenclature)
    ),

    Partner = trimws(
      as.character(Partner)
    ),

    ReporterISON = trimws(
      as.character(ReporterISON)
    ),

    PartnerISON = trimws(
      as.character(PartnerISON)
    ),

    latest_year_flag = as.integer(
      latest_year_flag
    ),

    MinStartYear = as.integer(
      MinStartYear
    ),

    MaxEndYear = as.integer(
      MaxEndYear
    ),

    ntm_all = as.numeric(
      ntm_all
    )
  )
#Do the same for the crosswalk
crosswalk_for_join <- itpd_crosswalk_final %>%
  transmute(
    HS6 = str_pad(
      trimws(as.character(HS6)),
      width = 6,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    ),

    itpd_description
  )

#See if everything looks right before (check NA)
source_validation <- us_ntms %>%
  summarise(
    total_rows = n(),

    missing_HS6 = sum(
      is.na(HS6) | HS6 == ""
    ),

    missing_NTMCode = sum(
      is.na(NTMCode) | NTMCode == ""
    ),

    missing_start_year = sum(
      is.na(MinStartYear)
    ),

    missing_end_year = sum(
      is.na(MaxEndYear)
    ),

    invalid_period = sum(
      MinStartYear > MaxEndYear,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    missing_ntm_all = sum(
      is.na(ntm_all)
    ),

    negative_ntm_all = sum(
      ntm_all < 0,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )

print(source_validation) #all zeros

#The researcher database states that the column with "latest_year_flag" is a binary indicator to denote the year in which the data is current. Keep it. 
us_ntmsSPS_TBT <- us_ntms %>%
  filter(
    latest_year_flag == 1,
    HSNomenclature == "H4",
    HS6 %in% crosswalk_for_join$HS6,
    str_detect(NTMCode, "^[AB]"),#A,B are indicators for SPS and TBT
    !is.na(MinStartYear),
    !is.na(MaxEndYear),
    !is.na(ntm_all),
    MinStartYear <= MaxEndYear
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ntm_type = case_when(
      str_starts(NTMCode, "A") ~ "SPS", #identifies the variables of interest
      str_starts(NTMCode, "B") ~ "TBT", #identifies the variables of interest
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    crosswalk_for_join,
    by = "HS6",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  )

#Given the nature of the source dataset, the code from above most likely result in identical observations, so remove them
ntm_source_unique <- us_ntmsSPS_TBT %>%
  distinct(
    ReporterISON,
    PartnerISON,
    Partner,
    HS6,
    NTMCode,
    MinStartYear,
    MaxEndYear,
    itpd_description,
    ntm_type,
    ntm_all
  )

nrow(us_ntmsSPS_TBT) - nrow(ntm_source_unique)

#Create the panel
ntm_active <- ntm_source_unique %>%
  filter(
    MinStartYear <= 2022, #max year
    MaxEndYear >= 2012 #min year
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    first_active_year = pmax(
      MinStartYear,
      2012L
    ),
    last_active_year = pmin(
      MaxEndYear,
      2022L
    )
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    year = list(
      seq.int(
        first_active_year,
        last_active_year
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  unnest(year) %>%
  ungroup()

#Compute the counts. note that I am using "ntm_all", as it is the column with the total of measures for a given product. 
#Counts
ntm_counts <- ntm_active %>%
  group_by(
    ReporterISON,
    Partner,
    year,
    itpd_description
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    count_SPS = sum(
      ntm_all[ntm_type == "SPS"]
    ),
    count_TBT = sum(
      ntm_all[ntm_type == "TBT"]
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    count_total = count_SPS + count_TBT
  )

#Check
ntm_counts %>%
  summarise(
    observations = n(),
    missing_SPS = sum(is.na(count_SPS)),
    missing_TBT = sum(is.na(count_TBT)),
    negative_SPS = sum(count_SPS < 0),
    negative_TBT = sum(count_TBT < 0)
  ) #all good

#Address the problem with the naming conventions that I had for the tariff data query. This problem will be explain in the code chunk for tariffs. 
ntm_counts <- ntm_counts %>%
  transmute(
    importer_iso3 = "USA",

    exporter_iso3 = case_when(
      Partner == "ZAR" ~ "COD", #current ISO used in WITS
      Partner == "ROM" ~ "ROU", #current ISO used in WITS
      Partner == "TMP" ~ "TLS", #current ISO used in WITS
      TRUE ~ Partner
    ),

    year = as.integer(year),

    itpd_description = trimws(
      as.character(itpd_description)
    ),

    count_SPS,
    count_TBT,
    count_total
  )

#verify
ntm_counts %>%
  filter(
    exporter_iso3 %in% c(
      "COD", "ROU", "TLS"
    )
  ) %>%
  distinct(exporter_iso3)
ntm_counts %>%
  filter(
    exporter_iso3 %in% c(
      "ZAR", "ROM", "TMP"
    )
  ) %>%
  distinct(exporter_iso3)#all good

#Make sure that the panel has the same data types
#Rename first
us_trade_panel<-us_trade_panel %>%
  rename(itpd_description=industry_descr)
us_trade_panel <- us_trade_panel %>%
  mutate(
    importer_iso3 = trimws(
      as.character(importer_iso3)
    ),
    exporter_iso3 = trimws(
      as.character(exporter_iso3)
    ),
    year = as.integer(year),
    itpd_description = trimws(
      as.character(itpd_description)
    )
  )

#Are there any missing combinations?
missing_ntm_combinations <- us_trade_panel %>%
  distinct(
    importer_iso3,
    exporter_iso3,
    year,
    itpd_description
  ) %>%
  anti_join( #the anti_join helps to identify them
    ntm_counts,
    by = c(
      "importer_iso3",
      "exporter_iso3",
      "year",
      "itpd_description"
    )
  )

nrow(missing_ntm_combinations) #there are 11044 missing

missing_ntm_combinations %>%
  count(exporter_iso3, sort = TRUE)

missing_ntm_combinations %>%
  count(itpd_description, sort = TRUE)

missing_ntm_combinations %>%
  count(year, sort = TRUE)

#There are missing because ntm_counts was generated from positive NTM records. Thus, a combination with neither an SPS nor TBT record did not generate a row.
#Create explicit zero_count combinations while merging
ntm_counts_complete <- us_trade_panel %>%
  distinct(
    importer_iso3,
    exporter_iso3,
    year,
    itpd_description
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    ntm_counts,
    by = c(
      "importer_iso3",
      "exporter_iso3",
      "year",
      "itpd_description"
    ),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ntm_match_status = case_when(
      !is.na(count_SPS) | !is.na(count_TBT) ~
        "Recorded NTM combination",

      importer_iso3 == exporter_iso3 ~
        "Domestic trade: assigned zero", #there is USA-USA trade in the ITPDE

      TRUE ~
        "No recorded SPS/TBT: assigned zero"
    ),

    count_SPS = replace_na(count_SPS, 0),#taking care of the missing
    count_TBT = replace_na(count_TBT, 0),#taking care of the missing
    count_total = count_SPS + count_TBT
  )

#now the actual merge
estimation_panel <- us_trade_panel %>%
  left_join(
    ntm_counts_complete,
    by = c(
      "importer_iso3",
      "exporter_iso3",
      "year",
      "itpd_description"
    ),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )
#Check
estimation_panel %>%
  summarise(
    observations = n(),
    missing_SPS = sum(is.na(count_SPS)),
    missing_TBT = sum(is.na(count_TBT)),
    missing_total = sum(is.na(count_total)),
    negative_SPS = sum(count_SPS < 0),
    negative_TBT = sum(count_TBT < 0)
  ) #all good

#DONE
write.csv(
  estimation_panel,
  "trade_NTMs"
)
```


```{r}
#Now clean the tariff data. Note: I will use AHS tariff rates at the HS-06 level. Analogous to the NTM data, I will group by industry and compute an average rate. Additionally, I will use MFN tariff rates for exporterxyearxindustry combinations that do not have an AHS rate. Important distinction: MFN rates do not vary by exporter, just by product. 
#See all the HS codes that being studied. Refer to the crosswalk as before. 
itpd_crosswalk_final <- itpd_crosswalk_final %>%
  mutate(
    HS6 = str_pad(as.character(HS6), width = 6, side = "left", pad = "0")
  )
hs_codes_WITS <- paste(
  unique(na.omit(itpd_crosswalk_final$HS6)),
  collapse = ","
)
writeClipboard(hs_codes_WITS) #this adds a copy to windows so I can paste into WITS for data extraction. 
#Do the same thing for countries, but now refering to the estimation panel. 
country_codes_WITS <- paste(
  unique(na.omit(estimation_panel$exporter_iso3)),
  collapse = ","
)
writeClipboard(country_codes_WITS)
#Note: WITS did not accept the ISO3 codes for: COD,MNE,ROU,SRB,TLS. Source: https://wits.worldbank.org/wits/WITS/WITSHELP/Content/Codes/Country_Codes.htm
#COD->ZAR "Democratic Republic of Congo"
#ROU->ROM "Romania"
#TLS->TMP "Timor-Leste/East Timor"
#MNE,SRB are reported jointly by WITS. Decision: drop observations for those. 
estimation_panel <- estimation_panel %>%
  filter(!exporter_iso3 %in% c("MNE", "SRB"))
#Note: when querying the data, select "TRAINS" as the data source, as it allows to include AVE equivalents using the "UNCTAD Method". 
tariff_raw<-read.csv("tariff_data.csv")
head(tariff_raw,10000)
tariff_raw <- tariff_raw %>%
  rename(HS6 = Product,
         year = Tariff.Year)
#Leading zeros
tariff_raw <- tariff_raw %>%
  mutate(
    HS6 = str_pad(as.character(HS6), width = 6, side = "left", pad = "0")
  )
#Assign industries
tariff_raw <- tariff_raw %>%
  left_join(
    itpd_crosswalk_final %>%
      select(HS6, itpd_description) %>%
      distinct(),
    by = "HS6",
    relationship ="many-to-many"
  )

#Filter the data. Retain only AHS since the BND are rate ceilings, which are not relevant for this project.The MFN data comes from a different download.  
unique(tariff_raw$DutyType)
tariff_AHS <- tariff_raw %>%
  filter(!DutyType %in% c("MFN","BND"))
head(tariff_AHS,10000)
head(estimation_panel)
#Before merging, note that there is no ISO3 code column available. See if the partner names match the main panel. 

all(tariff_AHS$Partner.Name %in% estimation_panel$exporter_name) #FALSE
setdiff(
  unique(estimation_panel$exporter_name),
  unique(tariff_AHS$Partner.Name)
)

      TRUE ~ exporter_iso3
    )
  )

tariff_AHS %>%

  distinct(exporter_iso3)
#Verify that all the ISO codes are contained in the estimation panel. 
all(tariff_AHS$exporter_iso3 %in% estimation_panel$exporter_iso3) #TRUE

#Now, calculate the simple averages per industry, so they can be later merged. library(dplyr)

tariffs_industry <- tariff_AHS %>%
  group_by(
    year,
    exporter_iso3,
    itpd_description
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    tariff_simple_average = if (
      all(is.na(Simple.Average))
    ) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(Simple.Average, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    number_hs_codes = n_distinct(HS6),
    hs_codes_with_tariff = n_distinct(
      HS6[!is.na(Simple.Average)]
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
#Example
tariffs_industry %>%
  filter(
    year == 2012,
    exporter_iso3 == "CAN"
  ) %>%
  arrange(itpd_description) %>%
  View()
head(tariffs_industry)
sum(is.na(tariffs_industry$tariff_simple_average))
#There are 135 values with NA. I will use the MFN rates to solve this issue later. Note: the MFN rates are for each HS x year, meaning that they do not vary by exporter. 

#Now, merge to the estimation panel. 

estimation_panel <- estimation_panel %>%
  left_join(
    tariffs_industry %>%
      select(
        year,
        exporter_iso3,
        itpd_description,
        tariff_simple_average
      ),
    by = c(
      "year",
      "exporter_iso3",
      "itpd_description"
    ),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )

head(estimation_panel) #Good, now it is time to take care of the missing rates. 
#Checkpoint: 
write.csv(
  estimation_panel,
  "trade_panel_ntms_ahs.csv"
)
```


```{r}
#Now, solve the missing tariffs issue. First, load the mfn data. 
mfn2012<-read.csv("mfn2012.csv")
mfn2013<-read.csv("mfn2013.csv")
mfn2014<-read.csv("mfn2014.csv")
mfn2015<-read.csv("mfn2015.csv")
mfn2016<-read.csv("mfn2016.csv")
mfn2017<-read.csv("mfn2017.csv")
mfn2018<-read.csv("mfn2018.csv")
mfn2019<-read.csv("mfn2019.csv")
mfn2020<-read.csv("mfn2020.csv")
mfn2021<-read.csv("mfn2021.csv")
mfn2022<-read.csv("mfn2022.csv")

mfn_all <- bind_rows(
  mfn2012,
  mfn2013,
  mfn2014,
  mfn2015,
  mfn2016,
  mfn2017,
  mfn2018,
  mfn2019,
  mfn2020,
  mfn2021,
  mfn2022
)
#leading zeros
mfn_all <- mfn_all %>%
  mutate(
    ProductCode = str_pad(as.character(ProductCode), width = 6, side = "left", pad = "0")
  )

#Rename to make it easier
mfn_all <- mfn_all %>%
  rename(HS6 = ProductCode,
         year = Year)

#Assign industries
mfn_all <- mfn_all %>%
  left_join(
    itpd_crosswalk_final %>%
      select(HS6, itpd_description) %>%
      distinct(),
    by = "HS6",
    relationship ="many-to-many"
  )
head(mfn_all)

#Analogous aggregation by industry. 
mfn_industries <- mfn_all %>%
  group_by(
    year,
    itpd_description
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    tariff_simple_average = if (
      all(is.na(SimpleAverage))
    ) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(SimpleAverage, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    number_hs_codes = n_distinct(HS6),
    hs_codes_with_tariff = n_distinct(
      HS6[!is.na(SimpleAverage)]
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
unique(mfn_all$itpd_description) #there is an NA here because the data had hs codes that are outside of the scope of this project. Nevertheless, see if all the values in the estimation panel exist in this dataset. 
all(estimation_panel$itpd_description %in% mfn_industries$itpd_description) #True, so all good. 
#Note: I am doing all of this with the MFN rates so I can populate the NA values that the AHS tariffs left in the estimation panel. Lets do that. 

mfn_industries %>%
  count(year, itpd_description) %>%
  filter(n > 1) #one observation per year x industry. 

estimation_panel <- estimation_panel %>%
  left_join(
    mfn_industries %>%
      select(
        year,
        itpd_description,
        mfn_tariff = tariff_simple_average #renames the column. It prevents R from creating confusing names because this column name already exists in the estimation panel.
      ),
    by = c("year", "itpd_description"), #matching variables
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    tariff_source = case_when(
      !is.na(tariff_simple_average) ~ "AHS", #if the original tariff is not missing, this labels it as AHS, so the original AHS tariff is retained. 
      is.na(tariff_simple_average) & !is.na(mfn_tariff) ~ "MFN replacement", #this part labels the tariff rate that comes from MFN as the replacement
      TRUE ~ "Missing"
    ),
    tariff_simple_average = coalesce(
      tariff_simple_average,
      mfn_tariff
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-mfn_tariff) #After mfn_tariff has been used to fill missing observations, this removes the temporary column.

#coalesce() operates as follows:
#If estimation_panel$tariff_simple_average is available, it remains unchanged.
#If it is NA, R uses the corresponding tariff from mfn_industries.
#If both values are NA, the result remains NA.

head(estimation_panel,10000)
sum(is.na(estimation_panel$tariff_simple_average))

#which are still missing
missing_tariffs <- estimation_panel %>%
  filter(is.na(tariff_simple_average)) %>%
  distinct(
    exporter_iso3,
    year,
    itpd_description
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    exporter_iso3,
    year,
    itpd_description
  )
#All the missing values come from the industry "eggs". The PPML will drop the rows that have this issue, which are 617 observations. This amount represents 0.0195% (617/31,634 observations) of all the panel. Since the percentage is very low, just let R drop them when making the calculations. Thus, the data construction process is done. Now, move to the estimation step. This will be included in the methodology section when describing the unique dataset.

estimation_panel <- estimation_panel %>%
  filter(exporter_iso3 != importer_iso3) #get rid of domestic trade


estimation_panel %>%
  summarise(
    observations       = n(),
    missing_trade      = sum(is.na(trade)),
    missing_SPS        = sum(is.na(count_SPS)),
    missing_TBT        = sum(is.na(count_TBT)),
    missing_tariff     = sum(is.na(tariff_simple_average)),
    negative_trade     = sum(trade < 0),
    negative_SPS       = sum(count_SPS < 0),
    negative_TBT       = sum(count_TBT < 0),
    inconsistent_total = sum(
      count_total != count_SPS + count_TBT
    )
  )


#get rid of the extra columns
colnames(estimation_panel)
estimation_panel <- estimation_panel %>% select(-X)

write.csv(
  estimation_panel,
  "final_panel.csv"
)
estimation_panel<-read.csv("final_panel.csv")


```


```{r}
#Now, estimate the PPML. Before estimation, convert tariffs into decimals
estimation_panel <- estimation_panel %>%
  mutate(
    tariff_decimal = tariff_simple_average / 100)

#Now with the model
m_pooled <- fepois(
  trade ~ log1p(tariff_decimal) +
          log1p(count_SPS) + log1p(count_TBT)|
          itpd_description^year +
          exporter_iso3^itpd_description +
          exporter_iso3^year,
  cluster = ~ exporter_iso3,
  data = estimation_panel
)
etable(m_pooled)

#Notes: Clustering by exporter allows arbitrary correlation among observations belonging to the same exporter while continuing to treat different exporters as independent clusters. Canada observations may be correlated with other Canada observations. Mexico observations may be correlated with other Mexico observations. Canada and Mexico are treated as separate clusters.

#Note that the fixed effects simplified logic: 

#itpd_description^year absorbs global industry-specific shocks or changing demand patterns over time. 
#exporter_iso3^itpd_description becomes exporter fixed effects. Absorbs time-invariant bilateral trade costs specific to that industry
#exporter_iso3^year absorbs global industry-specific shocks or changing demand patterns over time.


#Now lets look at OECD vs non_OECD countries
oecd_iso3 <- c(
  "AUS", "AUT", "BEL", "CAN", "CHL", "COL", "CRI",
  "CZE", "DNK", "EST", "FIN", "FRA", "DEU", "GRC",
  "HUN", "ISL", "IRL", "ISR", "ITA", "JPN", "KOR",
  "LVA", "LTU", "LUX", "MEX", "NLD", "NZL", "NOR",
  "POL", "PRT", "SVK", "SVN", "ESP", "SWE", "CHE",
  "TUR", "GBR", "USA"
)

estimation_sample <- estimation_panel %>%
  mutate(
    oecd_group = if_else(
      exporter_iso3 %in% oecd_iso3,
      "OECD",
      "Non-OECD"
    )
  )

#Check classification
estimation_sample %>%
  distinct(exporter_iso3, exporter_name, oecd_group) %>%
  arrange(oecd_group, exporter_iso3) %>%
  View()

#Estimate the OECD model
m_oecd <- fepois(
  trade ~ log1p(tariff_decimal) +
          log1p(count_SPS) +
          log1p(count_TBT) |
          itpd_description^year +
          exporter_iso3^itpd_description +
          exporter_iso3^year,
  cluster = ~ exporter_iso3,
  data = estimation_sample %>%
    filter(oecd_group == "OECD")
)

#now the non-OECD model 
m_non_oecd <- fepois(
  trade ~ log1p(tariff_decimal) +
          log1p(count_SPS) +
          log1p(count_TBT) |
          itpd_description^year +
          exporter_iso3^itpd_description +
          exporter_iso3^year,
  cluster = ~ exporter_iso3,
  data = estimation_sample %>%
    filter(oecd_group == "Non-OECD")
)

#Display them side-by-side
etable(m_pooled,m_oecd,m_non_oecd,
       tex = TRUE,
       headers = c("All Countries", "OECD Countries", "Non-OECD Countries"))

#This is the heart of the thesis.  
```


```{r}

library(modelsummary)
#Start with the modelling of the heterogeneous effects between agricultural industries. It is to be determined if these models will be included in the main paper or as an appendix. 
unique(estimation_sample$itpd_description)
industries<-unique(estimation_sample$itpd_description)
industries<-as.data.frame(industries)
industries
#Lets run three models for each broad group, as defined in the paper:
#Larch, M., Luckstead, J., & Yotov, Y. V. (2024). Economic sanctions and agricultural trade. American Journal of Agricultural Economics, 106(4), 1477-1517.. A pooled one, OECD, and non-OECD. First map them
library(dplyr)
unique(estimation_sample$itpd_description)
unique(estimation_sample$aggregated_sector)
estimation_sample <- estimation_sample %>%
  mutate(
    aggregated_sector = case_when(
      
      itpd_description %in% c(
        "Wheat",
        "Rice (raw)",
        "Corn",
        "Other cereals",
        "Cereal products",
        "Soybeans",
        "Other oilseeds (excluding peanuts)",
        "Animal feed ingredients and pet foods",
        "Pulses and legumes, dried, preserved",
        "Cotton"
      ) ~ "Bulk commodities",
      
      itpd_description %in% c(
        "Raw and refined sugar and sugar crops",
        "Other sweeteners"
      ) ~ "Sugars",
      
      itpd_description %in% c(
        "Fresh fruit",
        "Fresh vegetables",
        "Nuts",
        "Cocoa and cocoa products"
      ) ~ "Labor-intensive crops",
      
      itpd_description %in% c(
        "Prepared fruits and fruit juices",
        "Prepared vegetables",
        "Beverages, nec",
        "Tobacco leaves and cigarettes",
        "Spices",
        "Other agricultural products, nec"
      ) ~ "Processed foods",
      
      itpd_description %in% c(
        "Live Cattle",
        "Live Swine",
        "Eggs",
        "Other meats, livestock products, and live animals"
      ) ~ "Live animals, meat, and animal products",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

#1) Bulk commodities

m_bulkcommodities <- estimation_sample %>%
  filter(aggregated_sector == "Bulk commodities") %>%
  fepois(
    trade ~ log1p(tariff_decimal) +
            log1p(count_SPS) +
            log1p(count_TBT) |
            exporter_iso3^year + 
      exporter_iso3^itpd_description + itpd_description^year,
    cluster = ~ exporter_iso3,
    data = .
  )
etable(m_bulkcommodities)

m_bulkcommodities_OECD <- estimation_sample %>%
  filter(aggregated_sector == "Bulk commodities",
         oecd_group == "OECD") %>%
  fepois(
    trade ~ log1p(tariff_decimal) +
            log1p(count_SPS) +
            log1p(count_TBT) |
            exporter_iso3^year + 
      exporter_iso3^itpd_description + itpd_description^year,
    cluster = ~ exporter_iso3,
    data = .
  )
etable(m_bulkcommodities_OECD)

m_bulkcommodities_noOECD <- estimation_sample %>%
  filter(aggregated_sector == "Bulk commodities",
         oecd_group == "Non-OECD") %>%
  fepois(
    trade ~ log1p(tariff_decimal) +
            log1p(count_SPS) +
            log1p(count_TBT) |
            exporter_iso3^year + 
      exporter_iso3^itpd_description + itpd_description^year,
    cluster = ~ exporter_iso3,
    data = .
  )
etable(m_bulkcommodities_noOECD)
#Note that only the tariff variable had enough variation to show a coefficient. Let's create a table that show the three models. 
etable(m_bulkcommodities, m_bulkcommodities_OECD, m_bulkcommodities_noOECD, 
       tex = TRUE,
       headers = c("All Countries", "OECD Countries", "Non-OECD Countries"))
#I will change the name of the variable when the tables are exported into the thesis, for aesthetic purposes. 
#I will run the remaining models in one chunk each, so it is easier to follow.
```
